fns.desc: proc_coord_receive: `os_memcpy(tmp, pos, end - pos)` copies into a fixed `char tmp[20]` with NO check that `end - pos` fits. `end - pos` is the trailing path component of the SENDER's own sockaddr_un.sun_path (from recvmsg's msg_name), bounded only by UNIX_PATH_MAX (~108 bytes on Linux) via the earlier prefix check at :361-362, which verifies the path starts with pc->dir but places no limit on what follows it. Any local peer that can bind a Unix-domain socket under (or with a name starting with) pc->dir with a long trailing filename after the last '/' overflows this 20-byte stack buffer. Compounding bug: even when `end-pos` <= 19, the memcpy never NUL-terminates tmp before `atoi(tmp)` is called at :376, so atoi reads past the copied bytes into uninitialized stack memory looking for a terminator. Neither sub-issue is flagged by any of the 51 findings in this batch for this file.
